title: Multi‑tier spot‑blend routing with per‑tenant spend fences and accelerated fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers running latency-sensitive workloads need predictable spend and SLOs even when the platform uses spot instances or lower-tier GPUs to save cost. Current router heuristics prefer cheapest available capacity and sometimes cause tenant spend bursts or severe tail-latency when many spot evictions happen simultaneously.

Goal: Implement a multi-tier 'spot-blend' router that hedges requests across spot and on-demand pools while enforcing per-tenant soft and hard spend fences. The router should prefer cheaper capacity when safe, maintain latency SLOs, and gracefully degrade to fallback model variants (quantized / smaller model) before violating tenant hard spend caps.

Key features / acceptance criteria:
- Per-tenant spend fences: soft limit (alerts, progressive throttling) and hard limit (block or fall back to degraded variant).
- Tiered pools: Region->Tier->Instance class ranking. Router picks across pools with probabilistic hedging to reduce correlated preemptions.
- GPU type preference: allow tenant policy to prefer accelerator classes (A100, H100, L4) with cost-weighted scoring.
- Eviction hedging: when spot eviction risk > threshold, route a fraction to on-demand to keep latency P99 within target.
- Model variant fallback: automatically switch to approved cheaper/quantized model variants if continued routing to cheaper capacity would exceed hard fence or if latency SLOs degrade.
- Telemetry: expose token-level cost estimate, predicted spend delta for routing change, eviction rate, and per-tenant soft/hard fence breach counts in Console.
- Tests: e2e simulation with synthetic eviction patterns, integration with cost billing estimates, and canary rollout with 5% of tenants.

Design notes: Router will compute a routing_score = alpha * normalized_latency_budget + beta * normalized_cost + gamma * eviction_risk + delta * tenant_headroom where weights are configurable per-tenant or per-project. A stochastic component randomly selects some requests to on-demand to act as a hedge; the hedge fraction is adaptive: increases when eviction_risk rises or when soft fence is close. When hard fence is reached, router triggers model-variant fallback and increases hedging to on-demand 100% for SLO-critical requests.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Library: implement scoring and hedging algorithm as a library inside router-service (2w).
2) Enforcement: wire per-tenant spend fence lookup and counters from billing-store (1w).
3) Fallback paths: add model-variant resolution and tagging in catalog + runtime acceptance (1w).
4) Telemetry & Console: dashboard tiles + alerts (1w).
5) Canary & roll: 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with rollback playbook (1w).

Acceptance tests:
- Inject synthetic spot eviction patterns and verify P95/P99 latency stays within 1.25x baseline for hedged tenants.
- Simulate tenant hitting soft fence: observe progressive throttling and alert generation.
- Simulate tenant hitting hard fence: observe model fallback and billing estimate not exceeding hard fence for duration of test.
- Validate telemetry shows predicted vs actual spend within 10% during canary.

Rollout plan / monitoring:
- Start with internal tenants and low-risk customers flagged opt-in.
- Metrics to monitor: per-tenant spend projection, eviction rate, hedging fraction, fallback events, P95/P99 latency, cost per token.
- Pager rules: >3 hard-fence fallback events across any 5% cohort in a 15min window triggers SRE paging.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Spot+Blend+Router+Design
- Simulation harness (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim/pull/84
- Billing integration PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/209
- Console dashboard mockup: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/spot-blend-dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Soft/hard per-tenant spend fences enforced and configurable via tenant policy
Adaptive hedging reduces correlated spot preemption tail events in simulation
Automatic model-variant fallback triggers on hard fence or sustained SLO degradation
Telemetry surfaces predicted spend and actual spend with <10% divergence during canary
Canary rollout completed without regressions for P95/P99 latency

implementation_notes: Expose Hedging config as feature flag: router.spot_blend.enabled
Billing store endpoint: /billing/v1/tenant_headroom returns projected_remaining_usd as float string
Model catalog must mark variants with resource_weight and quality_score for fallback decisioning
qa_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and stochastic selection (coverage > 90%)
Simulated eviction traces with 10k req/s sustained for 30min in staging
Canary with 5% of tenants for 48h, validate telemetry and rollback criteria
Post-rollout regression suite for latency and cost anomalies
notes_for_ops: Rollback: disable router.spot_blend.enabled and revert tenant policies to baseline routing
Mitigation: increase hedging floor to 30% and temporarily mark high-risk regions as on-demand-only
Contact billing-oncall for spend anomalies: billing-oncall@redwood.ai
